summary: St. Joseph's North Pier range at the Michigan river mouth: the 1907 inner tower, the 1913 launch rescue, the 1955 razing of the mainland light, and city ownership since 2013.

lens.where: Fourth-order lens by Chance Brothers in the inner tower, 1907 (Michigan Lighthouse Conservancy; LighthouseFriends). The outer light carried a fifth-order lens.

structures.name: inner light
structures.note: Octagonal tower on a 24-foot square steel house, 57 ft (Michigan Lighthouse Conservancy); a fourth-order lens. LighthouseFriends describes the rear tower the same way.

structures.name: outer light
structures.note: Cylindrical tower on the pier, 35 ft, fifth-order lens (Michigan Lighthouse Conservancy; USLHS). LighthouseFriends describes a steel conical front tower of about 30 ft instead; the sources disagree.
Fog signal building integral with the inner tower; diaphone installed in the rear tower in 1933 (Michigan Lighthouse Conservancy; LighthouseFriends).
Duplex keepers' dwelling, seven rooms in each of two apartments, at the inner end of the north pier (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Reached through Tiscornia Beach (City). The Inner Light is open for tours on summer Saturdays, run by St. Joe Today (City).

facts.agency: City of St. Joseph (owner since 2013). The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers owns the North Pier; the U.S. Coast Guard operates the beacons (City).

keepers.name: George J. Cornell
keepers.note: The 1913 Bulletin names him as keeper of the St. Joseph Pierhead Light Station when he helped save the launch Wolverine on 14 July 1913.

keepers.name: Owen C. McCauley
keepers.note: In charge of the pierhead lights 1931-1936 and tried to save the mainland lighthouse (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: Daniel R. Platt
keepers.note: Head keeper of the mainland and pierhead lights, LighthouseFriends says; not on the archive's pierhead roster. The span is the mainland light's service, and the pier service is not dated separately.

wrecks.outcome: Saved from stranding after keeper George J. Cornell got a line to the boat as it drifted past the station; lifesavers brought it into harbor.
The Board's 1899 report records a new spar set up to locate the wreck at the pier range; the date and cause of the loss are not given in the source read.

corrections.current: St. Joseph North Pier Outer Light
corrections.proposed: St. Joseph North Pier Inner and Outer Lights
corrections.why: The id and the story are about the inner light of a two-light range. The name records only the outer light. The National Register name and the city's page name both lights.

1846 is the archive's establishment year for the range (USLHS). The first lighthouse was 1832 (LighthouseFriends; Michigan Lighthouse Conservancy). The inner light, the one this record describes, was first lit in 1907; the outer light in 1906.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The USLHS record gives 1846; LighthouseFriends and the Michigan Lighthouse Conservancy date the first lighthouse to 1832. The story gives 1832 for the first lighthouse and 1906-07 for the present range, and notes the archive's 1846 date.

LighthouseFriends describes the front tower as a steel conical tower of about 30 feet with a fifth-order lens. The Michigan Lighthouse Conservancy describes the outer light as a cast-iron cylinder of 35 feet, first lit 1906. Not reconciled; the story says the sources disagree.

The archive record says 'Active Aid to Navigation? No'. The City of St. Joseph says the lights are still active aids to navigation, with the beacons operated by the Coast Guard. The story states both; not reconciled.

notes_for_editor: The NRHP nomination (05001211) is not digitised at NPGallery: the fetch returned the placeholder. Wikipedia was read for leads only: its infobox and its statement that the 1859 light was demolished in 1955 match LighthouseFriends, and no Wikipedia claim is cited. The Michigan Lighthouse Conservancy page is cited through its archived copy. The Board's pier entries were cited by scan page, because the printed page could not be confirmed. The 1891 'about midway' and 'bell is ineffective' passages were matched on scan page 497. The 1913 storm is named in the Bulletin's December 1913 article 'Storm on Great Lakes' (PDF p.45): the severe storm of 8-10 November 1913. Roster lines are matched by name and position (0.14 km). Owen C. McCauley appears twice, as head keeper 1931-1936 and first assistant 1928-1931. Daniel R. Platt has no archive person slug. A Chronicling America search for St. Joseph pierhead keepers in Michigan papers, 1900-1935, returned nothing. The record's name ('Outer Light') and id ('inner') disagree; see corrections. The record's outer-tower height 9.0 m is not the 35 ft (10.7 m) that the Conservancy gives; the LighthouseFriends front tower is about 30 ft. The 1895 Board volume's OCR gives the report's fiscal year as 'June 30, 1896', but its letter is dated 9 November 1895 and its running heads read 1895; the story says 'the Board's report for 1895'. The 1895 entry is at scan pages 341 (and 351, a repeat).
